fitnessSpec.day: Full alpine start-to-finish day — the FA took roughly 11 hours
fitnessSpec.climb: Sustained technical slab climbing to 5.13- with limited/insecure protection

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~1.5–2.5 hrs from the SR-20 hairpin pullout (East Face climbers' trail) to the East Face base (shares approach and first 3 pitches with Freedom or Death)
requiredSkills: Redpoint-level 5.13 slab technique on featureless rock
Long multi-pitch endurance and route-finding on a line where little detail is known
Self-sufficient bailing/retreat judgment (no documented repeat parties to reference)
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Elite 5.13 slab specialist with big multi-pitch mileage — a serious, committing objective

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very strenuous - trip reports cite roughly 4,500 ft gain over ~4.5 miles from the trailhead to the summit area, largely off-trail with a creek crossing and bushwhacking low down
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Most parties backpack in and camp near 6,600 ft before a summit push, so overnight pack weight (roughly 30-45 lbs) is typical rather than a single long day-pack push

partner_requirements.approachTime: Typically about 3 to 3.5 hours from the trailhead to high camp, then roughly 2 more hours from camp to Big Craggy's summit on its own (5 to 6 hours when West Craggy is climbed first); commonly done as a 2-day trip
requiredSkills: Class 3 scrambling on notably loose rock
off-trail route-finding and navigation (GPS strongly recommended)
wilderness backcountry camping/self-sufficiency (no facilities, self-issued permit)
judgment around rockfall - no technical rope/glacier skills needed since there is no glacier travel
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid Class 3 scrambling experience with comfort on loose, moving rock; should have done other loose-rock NE Cascades/Pasayten-style scrambles before this one

partner_requirements.fitnessSpec: Grade covers a powerful ~100 ft roof pitch plus loose 5.2 terrain lower on the route
requiredSkills: Roof/overhang crack technique on the roof pitch
Comfort on loose rock on the first pitch and a loose block at the start of the roof
Strong second recommended — documented pendulum-fall hazard pulling gear through the roof
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Confident 5.10 trad leader

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong, sustained hiking fitness for a long wilderness approach (Pete Lake Trail plus off-trail climber's path and glacier travel) with significant elevation gain in a single push or over an overnight backpack.
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Moderate-heavy: overnight/bivy gear (many parties camp near Pete Lake or higher to break up the long approach), a rock rack, glacier kit (rope, harness, crevasse-rescue hardware), and helmet for rockfall.

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long approach: roughly 4-6 miles one-way on the Pete Lake Trail to Pete Lake (~2,980 ft) followed by an off-trail climber's path and lower Chimney Glacier crossing to the foot of the rock; exact hour count not confirmed in sources, but the approach alone is commonly broken into an overnight backpack rather than done car-to-car in one push.
requiredSkills: Leading wet, loose fourth-class rock and building anchors from stoppers and slings
Basic glacier travel and crevasse rescue (roped crossing of the Chimney Glacier on approach)
Route-finding on an unmarked climber's path and broken alpine terrain
Rockfall awareness/management in the chimney systems
Self-sufficiency for a long, remote day with no reliable outside help nearby
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine climber comfortable leading wet, loose fourth-class rock in a remote setting and rappelling off self-built anchors, with prior glacier-travel and self-rescue experience; not a beginner objective given the long approach, the moat crossing and the rockfall-prone gully.

partner_requirements.approachTime: No route-specific approach time found; standard South Buttress car-to-car reports range ~8.5–15 hrs depending on party speed/pitching style
requiredSkills: Off-trail routefinding/contouring southeast from ~6,500 ft to reach the buttress — no established trail
Judgment to inspect and back up questionable fixed rappel anchors (tat on 2 half-rope raps into gaps/cols)
3rd/4th-class and easy 5th-class simul-travel for a long day
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Alpine rock party comfortable with a long day (Grade III+, ~1,200 ft / 22 pitches vs. 850 ft / 12 pitches for the standard line)

fitnessSpec.hiking: Moderate-good fitness; trip reports cite roughly 6 hours up and 4 hours down trailhead-to-trailhead
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light rack (small set plus slings) and scrambling gear, roughly 10-15 lb

partner_requirements.approachTime: Roughly 2-3 hours from the SR 20 pullout through meadows/the approach bowl to the ridge saddle; a 10-hour total route day starting early morning
requiredSkills: exposed scrambling
short 5.6 pitch leading
ridge route-finding
basic rope/anchor skills for the short technical steps near the summit
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Competent scrambler/easy-5th-class leader; good route-finding judgment needed since Class 4 variations easily wander onto harder terrain

fitnessSpec.day: Full-day alpine push in cold, shaded conditions
fitnessSpec.climb: Sustained 5.13+ face/crack climbing over 10 pitches, 1,100 ft

partner_requirements.approachTime: About 20 minutes from the SR-20 hairpin pullout east of Washington Pass
requiredSkills: Redpoint-level 5.13+ trad/face climbing
Comfort climbing in cold, perpetually shaded conditions
Long multi-pitch endurance and self-sufficient route-finding
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Elite free climber — WA's hardest documented multipitch free route (5.13+); realistically out of range for all but a handful of climbers

fitnessSpec.length: Short — 75 ft (23 m), typically climbed as part of a longer link-up via the Southwest Rib/Boving-Pollock variation

partner_requirements.approachTime: No route-specific approach time found; likely shares the Blue Lake Trail west-side approach (~1–1.5 hrs to basin, not confirmed for this line specifically)
requiredSkills: Offwidth/chimney technique, 1–2 ft wide
Minimal gear until near the top of the pitch (rated R)
Backpacks reportedly hauled separately at the belay given the chimney's width
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Real offwidth/chimney comfort with tolerance for sparse protection

partner_requirements.fitnessSpec: Long alpine day: Colchuck Lake TH to Witches Tower via Aasgard Pass documented as ~14 mi RT with ~5,400 ft gain, often done as a single 14+ hour push to avoid the Core Zone permit
partner_requirements.approachTime: Long day via Colchuck Lake and Aasgard Pass (Aasgard alone gains ~2,200 ft in ~0.9 mi)
requiredSkills: 3rd–4th class scrambling with a short, exposed slabby ledge
Basic mixed/ice competency if attempted with lingering snow/ice (route graded as low as Ice 2/M1b in early-season conditions)
Comfort with heavy exposure on all sides near the summit
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate — comfortable with 3rd–4th class scrambling and significant summit exposure; low-5th-class/mixed skill needed if snow/ice lingers

fitnessSpec.hiking: Big all-day objective -- the FA party took 14 hours car-to-car soloing almost the entire 3.5-mile ridge
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light/fast rack -- the FA party placed no protection and made only two short rappels

partner_requirements.approachTime: Via Cedar Creek Trailhead near Mazama -- distinct from the Silver Star Creek approach used for the standard Silver Star Glacier route on the same peak
requiredSkills: Soloing exposed 4th/low-5th class terrain
Independent route-finding on a long, multi-summit ridge
Loose-rock hazard management
Self-sufficiency far from rescue
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Advanced -- an experienced alpine rock party comfortable soloing sustained 4th/low-5th terrain for hours; the published route notes state plainly that if you think you need more specific beta, this is likely not the route for you.

partner_requirements.fitnessSpec: Multi-day approach with a roped Terror Glacier crossing and a long technical descent (6–14 rappels documented)
partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-day approach into Terror Basin via the Terror Glacier crossing
requiredSkills: Roped glacier travel with real crevasse/moat judgment (unstable snow bridges documented firsthand)
Solid 5.9 crack-climbing ability for the crux — a sustained ~30m hand/fist crack per a 2024 trip report
Tolerance for loose, runout lower pitches before reaching solid rock
Strong multi-rappel descent/anchor-building skill (6 double-length raps per a 2017 account; 14 rappels per a 2024 account, down the West Ridge/gully)
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Advanced — a serious multi-day alpine-rock commitment, not a beginner outing

fitnessSpec.hiking: Moderate - this is a short descent (roughly 3 hours), but demands sustained careful movement, not fitness.
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light - rope, rack, and whatever was carried up the ascent route.

partner_requirements.approachTime: N/A - reached only from the summit.
requiredSkills: efficient multi-rappel technique on natural anchors
confident, careful movement on loose, exposed, unroped 3rd/4th-class terrain
route-finding via cairns across rib crossings
sound judgment - this is exactly the kind of 'easy' terrain where fatal accidents happen from complacency
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate+ - technically easier than the peak's technical routes, but the loose, unprotectable, exposed nature makes it inappropriate for inexperienced scramblers.

fitnessSpec.approach: ~1 hr via Blue Lake Trail to base (general SEWS approach beta, not route-specific)

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~1 hour (Blue Lake Trail, general SEWS approach beta, not confirmed route-specific)
requiredSkills: Crux P2: wet vertical crack requiring gastons/deadpoints
Tolerance for lichen/loose debris typical of an underused line
Route joins the existing Mojo Rising line at its P5
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid 5.11 trad leader with thin-finger/seam-crack skill

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high; multi-day off-trail approach with sustained elevation gain and bushwhacking to reach high camp near Challenger Glacier/Luna Cirque before any climbing begins
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Heavy multi-day mountaineering load (bivy/camp gear, glacier kit, several days of food) — roughly 40-50 lb

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-day (commonly 2-3 days) from Ross Lake to a high camp in the Challenger Glacier/Luna Cirque area before the summit push, consistent with general Northern Pickets approach beta
requiredSkills: glacier travel and crevasse rescue
roped snow travel
Class 4 exposed scrambling on loose rock
off-trail route-finding and bushwhacking
self-sufficiency far from help (remoteness hazard)
multi-day backcountry camping
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine climbers only — this is not an entry-level objective. Partner should have prior glaciated-peak and off-trail Cascades experience before attempting a Northern Pickets summit.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Long, sustained off-trail approach through dense brush and steep forest with significant elevation gain from the Baker Lake basin; multi-day backcountry fitness expected
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight/multi-day pack (backcountry camping permit required for overnight stays), likely 30-40+ lbs including camp gear

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-day approach typical (same rugged Baker Lake / Blum Lakes country used for neighboring Bacon Peak and Mount Blum); no single-day trailhead-to-summit norm documented
requiredSkills: Off-trail navigation/routefinding among Hagan's several summits
Bushwhacking through dense approach vegetation
Class 2-3 scrambling on loose rock
Backcountry camping and Leave No Trace in a National Park setting
Self-sufficiency: remote location with no cell coverage and long evacuation times
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced off-trail scrambler comfortable with unmaintained, trail-less North Cascades terrain and multi-summit routefinding

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high; multi-day, trail-less approach with roughly 5,500 ft of elevation gain over brush, talus, and cross-country terrain to the Terror Basin camp
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Heavy overnight/glacier-travel kit (40-50+ lbs) for the multi-day approach plus a full alpine rock rack

partner_requirements.approachTime: 1-2 days of cross-country travel to reach the Terror Basin camp before the climb itself
requiredSkills: Multi-pitch traditional rock leading at 5.7 with sustained exposure
Route-finding on an unmarked, trail-less approach and on the ridge itself
Glacier travel and crevasse rescue (standard kit for this zone per outside route beta)
Efficient rappelling/downclimbing on loose alpine rock for the descent
Self-sufficient multi-day wilderness travel and navigation in a remote, no-rescue-nearby setting
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Advanced to expert alpine climbers only - prior remote North Cascades/Pickets-style objectives strongly recommended before this one

fitnessSpec.hiking: Moderate-high fitness for a roughly 7.5-mile round trip with about 2,700 ft of gain, often done car-to-car in a day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light day pack (water, layers, navigation) - no technical rack or overnight gear needed for the standard scramble

partner_requirements.approachTime: Roughly 2-3 hours from the Iron Peak trailhead to the saddle/scramble start, based on trip reports reaching the ridge saddle by mid-morning from a ~8am start
requiredSkills: off-trail routefinding
loose-rock scrambling judgment
basic navigation/map reading above the trail
afternoon-thunderstorm awareness and turnaround discipline
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Comfortable with off-trail Class 2 scrambling and basic routefinding; prior scrambling or peak-bagging experience recommended since the route leaves the maintained Iron Peak Trail onto open slopes

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very strenuous long day with a lot of undulating elevation gain/loss along the ridge above Blanca Lake; car-to-car pushes commonly run 10-12+ hours with a likely dark finish, so many parties instead camp at Virgin Lake and split it into an overnight
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight pack (~30-35 lb) if camping at Virgin Lake, or a lighter summit-day pack (~15-20 lb) with axe/crampons for a single-push attempt

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long: multi-hour approach via the Monte Cristo townsite area or North Fork Sauk/Sloan Creek side per prior research, often making this a two-day trip; treat it as a full alpine day even before the summit scramble begins
requiredSkills: Class 3 rock scrambling with real exposure
off-trail route-finding on a rugged, brushy climber's trail
basic snow travel and self-arrest
glacier-travel awareness for the early-season glacier remnant on Kyes' flanks
navigation for the remote Monte Cristo / Sloan Creek approach
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate scrambler comfortable with sustained Class 3 exposure and off-trail route-finding on a faint climber's trail; prior snow travel and basic glacier-travel awareness are strongly preferred given the early-season glacier remnant

fitnessSpec.stamina: Full alpine day — documented ascents range from a fast 13-hour "easy version" to a 5-hour partial traverse finishing after dark; total ~2,000 ft over 26 pitches (Grade V)
fitnessSpec.climbing: 5.9 trad, comfortable soloing/simul-climbing easier terrain to move quickly

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~1-2 hours via the Blue Lake Trail/climbers' path to the Beckey Route start on Liberty Bell; full traverse has taken documented parties anywhere from ~5 hours (partial, in poor conditions) to 13+ hours car-to-car
requiredSkills: Simul-climbing / fast multi-pitch systems
Multiple technical rappel transitions between towers
Route-finding across 5 distinct summits (Liberty Bell, Concord Tower, Lexington Tower, North Early Winter Spire, South Early Winter Spire)
Efficient anchor-building
Judgement to bail at a notch when conditions deteriorate — retreat means rappels and a loose gully
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Expert alpine climbers only — a full-day 5.9 enchainment across 5 summits demanding fast, efficient movement

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong multi-day backpacking fitness - the loop runs over 40 miles with more than 13,000 ft of gain across five days
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Multi-day wilderness pack (food/shelter/navigation for a several-day trip); no technical climbing gear required beyond standard scrambling kit

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long, multi-day approach - two days from the Robinson Creek trailhead over Robinson, Rolo and Shellrock passes to a camp below Butte Pass, with the summit climbed from there as part of a five-day loop that exits over Pistol Pass
requiredSkills: Off-trail Class 2 (locally Class 3/4 to bypass a summit snowfield) route-finding through talus and past false summits
Self-sufficient wilderness navigation - long, remote approach with no cell coverage or quick bail-out
Basic snow travel/kick-stepping for the summit snowfield when present
Self-rescue mindset given the extreme remoteness
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced wilderness backpacker/scrambler comfortable with multi-day off-trail travel far from help; described in trip reports as an 'unremarkable' Washington Top-100/Bulger peak usually combined with several other Pasayten summits in one trip, so partners should be prepared for a big multi-day itinerary, not a single-day tag

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strenuous, multi-day capability: several miles of maintained trail plus sustained off-trail travel over heather, scree, and possible snow patches to reach basin camp, then a ~5hr round-trip scramble day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight pack (roughly 30-40+ lbs) for the basin camp approach, plus a lighter summit-day pack

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-day: typically 1 day to establish basin camp via Cascade Pass and off-trail travel
requiredSkills: Class 3-4 scrambling with exposure tolerance
off-trail route-finding through slabs and benches (explicitly called out in existing beta)
basic navigation / map & compass or GPS competence for the unmaintained approach
judgment on wet-rock and loose-rock hazard
early-season snow travel competence if attempting near the front of the July window
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate to advanced scrambler — needs prior Class 3-4 scrambling mileage and comfort being unroped (or short-roped) on exposed, broken terrain; this is not a beginner objective given the off-trail approach and loose, corkscrewing summit ledges

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very strong - the trail alone is ~7.5 miles one-way with well over 5,000 ft of gain to its end, plus additional scrambling and elevation to the summit; most parties do this as an overnight rather than a huge single-push day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight pack (30-40+ lb) is typical since most parties camp near Heaton Camp given the remote, self-rescue-only access; a very fit team could attempt a light/fast single-push day

partner_requirements.approachTime: Full day to reach the scramble start (6.5-7.5 mi, well over 5,000 ft gain to trail's end/Heaton Camp); most parties treat this as a multi-day trip rather than a single push
requiredSkills: confident Class 3 scrambling on loose, exposed rock
route-finding above the trail's end (talus field then ledgy rock marked by old paint/arrows in places)
sound judgment managing exposure without a rope, or willingness to carry/place protection for the final block
self-rescue mindset - evacuation from this area is slow and remote
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced scrambler comfortable with sustained, loose Class 3 terrain and real exposure; several trip reports and NPS notes suggest a rope is advisable for the final summit block even though it's graded Class 3

requiredSkills: P1: 105 ft 5.11b/A0 with a runout 5.6 section below the first bolt
P2: thin flaring aid seam (5.6 C1+)
P3: 10a free mixed with C1 aid plus a wide-crack traverse
P4 'Skywalker Traverse' needs tension moves
P5 has a documented totally detached block
Rack: 2 sets small-medium cams, extra small nuts, 11+ draws
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Genuine aid competence required, not just strong 5.11 free climbing — the route has never been fully freed

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high endurance: reports cite roughly 7-9 hours trailhead-to-camp and another 5-7 hours camp to summit (roughly 10-13 hours round trip), over a long approach with elevation gain through the Anderson Pass area
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Heavy overnight glacier-climbing load (multi-day food/camp gear plus rope, harness, crevasse rescue kit, and ice axe/crampons) - expect a full mountaineering pack, not a light day load

partner_requirements.approachTime: Roughly 7-9 hours trailhead to camp, per available trip reports, with camp-to-summit taking an additional 5-7 hours one way (roughly 10-13 hours round trip) - a multi-day trip overall
requiredSkills: Roped glacier travel and crevasse rescue
Self-arrest and steep snow climbing technique (reported crux slopes now 40+ degrees at Flypaper Pass due to glacier recession)
Class 3 scrambling on loose summit rock
Multi-day wilderness backpacking / route-finding without maintained trail on the upper mountain
Wilderness permit and bear-canister logistics for Olympic National Park overnight travel
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced glacier mountaineer - comfortable with roped glacier travel, crevasse rescue, and steep snow climbing on a committing multi-day wilderness objective (not a beginner route)

fitnessSpec.hiking: 6+ mile approach each way to Upper Eagle Lake (per existing trail access) plus significant off-trail gain to the crest and summit gully — fit for a long, full car-to-car or high-camp summit day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light scrambling pack if day-tripping from a high camp; overnight gear if backpacking in, since most parties camp near Upper Eagle Lake given the approach length

partner_requirements.approachTime: Most parties treat this as a backpack with an early, pre-dawn summit push from high camp
requiredSkills: Class 3 scrambling on loose talus/scree
off-trail route-finding to the southern Sawtooth crest
self-arrest/steep-scree descent technique
backcountry water planning (limited water on the crest)
afternoon-thunderstorm awareness and turnaround discipline
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid Class 3 scrambler comfortable with loose rock and exposed, unmarked terrain; prior off-trail/cross-country navigation experience strongly recommended given the remote Sawtooth crest setting

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong, sustained fitness for a long off-trail approach through dense brush, plus stamina for glacier travel at altitude
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Moderate-heavy - overnight/multi-day capable pack carrying rope, crevasse rescue gear, and self-sufficient camping kit for a remote approach

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long and demanding - remote drainage approach with significant off-trail/bushwhack travel; many parties treat this as a multi-day trip (exact trailhead-to-glacier time not confirmed in sources)
requiredSkills: Roped glacier travel and crevasse rescue
Off-trail routefinding through dense brush with minimal trail
Self-sufficient wilderness travel/navigation (no reliable cell coverage)
Class 3 scrambling comfort with exposure
Sound judgment on committing, remote terrain far from rescue
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine climbers only - prior roped glacier travel and remote off-trail wilderness trips required; not suitable for a first alpine outing

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong multi-day hiking fitness; approach alone typically runs into double-digit miles from Dosewallips or Grand Valley trailheads to a high camp, per the very long approach
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight/multi-day pack weight (camp gear, food, navigation tools) for the standard high-camp approach

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long multi-hour-to-multi-day approach to a high camp in the Cameron Creek/Grand Pass area before the summit push; total route time from high camp is on the order of 10 hours round trip
requiredSkills: map/compass or GPS navigation on featureless open slopes and talus (no defined trail)
Class 2-3 scrambling movement, with comfort on occasional exposed steps
early-season snow travel / self-arrest awareness given lingering snow into summer
wilderness camping and Leave No Trace practice (permit required)
self-sufficient backcountry judgment given the long, remote approach and afternoon weather exposure
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid off-trail wilderness scrambler comfortable with sustained route-finding on open alpine terrain far from help; prior Class 2-3 scrambling and multi-day backcountry travel experience recommended

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong, sustained hiking fitness for the notoriously steep Lake Constance trail (~3,300 ft gain in about 2 miles), typically followed by an early pre-dawn summit push the next day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight pack (roughly 30-40 lbs) for the standard 2-day approach-then-summit itinerary, lighter summit-day pack for the push from camp

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~3-4 hrs on a very steep trail to Lake Constance camp; almost always climbed as a 2-day trip with a pre-dawn summit day
requiredSkills: confident, continuous exposed Class 3-4 scrambling/climbing with no fixed protection
route-finding through Avalanche Canyon and the upper gully/chimney system
composure crossing the Terrible Traverse and around the Cat's Ears at the South Chute notch
snow travel/self-arrest skills for lingering snow in the gullies, especially early in the season
judgment to turn around if rockfall risk or route-finding uncertainty increases
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate to advanced scrambler/climber. Prior experience on exposed Class 3-4 alpine terrain is expected; this is a serious undertaking for a first big scramble given the loose rock and the Terrible Traverse/Cat's Ears exposure noted in the existing beta.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high - multi-day approach of roughly 15-20+ miles one-way to a high camp near Marmot Lake or O'Neil Pass, with substantial elevation gain, before a separate summit day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Heavy multi-day/overnight pack (approach carries food, camp gear, and bear-resistant storage for several days)

partner_requirements.approachTime: Typically 2+ days each way to a high camp near Marmot Lake/O'Neil Pass via the Duckabush River or Dosewallips/Anderson Pass trails, plus a dedicated summit day - full trips commonly run 4-6+ days
requiredSkills: Off-trail routefinding on talus, heather, and benches to and above high camp
Steep snow travel and self-arrest (snow persists into early summer per watch-outs)
Short, exposed Class 3 scrambling near the summit
Map/compass or GPS navigation to identify the true high point among the multi-summit massif
Self-sufficient wilderness backpacking (remote, far from any road or help)
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced scrambler/backpacker with prior Class 3 and steep-snow experience; the long remote approach and multi-summit navigation make this a poor choice for a first scramble partner

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strenuous full day; roughly 8 miles and significant elevation gain if done car-to-car, or a shorter summit push if camped at Twin Lakes
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light day pack for the summit push; overnight pack if establishing the Twin Lakes camp described in the beta

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~2-3 hrs hiking in to Twin Lakes/High Pass area for a day trip; multi-day parties hike in and camp at Twin Lakes first, then face a shorter (~6 hr) summit day
requiredSkills: Class 3-4 scrambling on loose, blocky rock
Route-finding on ridge and gully terrain (staying on the more solid rib, avoiding the looser gully)
Rockfall awareness and helmet use - small party size recommended to reduce rockfall risk to others
Comfort with exposed summit moves
Basic snow travel/kick-stepping for lingering early-season snow near the ridge
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate to advanced scrambler; prior Class 3-4 scrambling experience strongly recommended given sustained loose rock and summit exposure

fitnessSpec.hiking: ~10 miles round trip with roughly 4,900 ft of gain via the Nason Ridge trail and meadows; a long full day on the ridge
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Standard day-scramble pack (~15-20 lb: water, layers, navigation, basic first aid) - no technical rack needed for this route

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~5 hours to the summit from the Merritt Lake trailhead (per on-the-ground trip reports), longer if combined with Mount Howard
requiredSkills: off-trail routefinding through heather and talus (trail thins above treeline)
steady footing on loose scree and steep heather slopes
basic exposure tolerance for narrow ridge sections
map/GPS navigation - route is not signed or continuously trailed
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate scrambler - comfortable with off-trail routefinding, loose talus, and short exposed Class 3 ridge moves; not a beginner hike despite the Class 2-3 grade

fitnessSpec.hiking: Expedition-level fitness — sustained multi-day travel with a loaded overnight pack over trail-less, uneven terrain (brush, talus, river-cut banks) to reach a high camp in the upper Elwha Basin before the scramble even begins.
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Multi-day overnight pack (roughly 35-45+ lbs with camp gear and food for the approach/high camp), plus a lighter summit-day kit for the scramble itself.

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long, remote, multi-day approach — typically requires establishing a high camp in the upper Elwha Basin before leaving trail for the summit scramble.
requiredSkills: off-trail routefinding on trail-less terrain
river fording technique and judgment
Class 3 scrambling with exposure
backcountry navigation (map/compass/GPS) without established trail
self-rescue / self-sufficiency given remote, multi-day evacuation distance
sound weather judgment for afternoon conditions
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced off-trail scrambler/mountaineer comfortable with self-directed routefinding in trail-less, remote wilderness; prior Olympic-interior or similar off-trail alpine experience strongly preferred given the long approach and lack of beta.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong - long approach (reports cite roughly 12-14 miles RT with 3,500-5,200 ft gain via the Snow Lake and Gem Lake trail corridor) plus sustained off-trail brush and talus travel
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light day-scramble kit only (helmet recommended for the loose gully, approach shoes or light boots, minimal overnight gear)

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long, multi-hour approach - forest and brush from the Snow Lake/Gem Lake corridor before the scramble even begins; treat as a full-day car-to-car objective
requiredSkills: solid Class 2-3 scrambling on loose rock and talus
route-finding through brushy, off-trail terrain with no maintained tread
comfort on exposed, essentially unprotectable rock (no gear placements in the crux gully)
sound judgment to retreat if rock is wet or route-finding gets uncertain
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced scrambler with prior unroped Class 3 exposure; not a beginner objective despite the modest elevation

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~2.5 hours car-to-base (one documented party: 7:30am trailhead departure, roped up ~10:00am); no established trail for the final stretch
requiredSkills: Loose, runout 5.7 PG13 pitch gaining the North Ridge Notch, protectable with only 1–2 marginal cams
Unprotected 5.6 slab climbing low on the route
Simul-climbing efficiency for a long day (documented car-to-car times range ~6–16 hrs)
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Alpine rock party comfortable with loose, runout low-fifth-class terrain

fitnessSpec.hiking: Long full car-to-car day (roughly 10-14 hrs): several miles of logging-road approach (often biked) plus ~1,500 ft of sustained scrambling each way
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light alpine day pack — helmet required, light rack/handline optional (some parties carry a rope for a hand-line on exposed sections even though most don't end up using it)

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~6-7 hrs trailhead to summit, 4-5 hrs summit to trailhead (bike recommended for the multi-mile logging-road approach); scrambling portion alone is at least ~3 hrs round trip
requiredSkills: Class 3-4 scrambling on exposed ridge crest
route-finding (staying on the correct side of the ridge, climber's left near the false summits — straying right there leads into unintended class 5 terrain per multiple trip reports)
comfort with loose rock/blocks
optional: mountain biking the logging-road approach
early-season: ice axe use for lingering snow
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced Class 3-4 scrambler comfortable on sustained exposed terrain; this is a step up from a beginner scramble — most parties do not rope up but should be capable of unroped movement over loose blocks and short class 4/occasional class 5 moves if they stray off-route

partner_requirements.fitnessSpec: Fit for a long, full-value day (~14.5-hr summit-and-exit day)
requiredSkills: Real snow/ice competence — self-arrest, crampon/axe on firm 30-40°+ approach couloir terrain that can hold firm snow/ice into July
Route-finding judgment — a ledge/gendarme maze near the top is repeatedly cited as the navigation crux
Brush/bushwhack tolerance on the Mountaineer Creek approach
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid 5.6 trad leader; 5.7 at the crag gives margin, since the crux can feel stiffer than its grade

fitnessSpec.hiking: Long summer day: approach via the PCT (from Snowgrass Flat, Berry Patch, or Chambers Lake trailheads) plus significant elevation gain before the final ridge scramble; fitness for a full, long trail day is required, though exact mileage/time was not independently re-verified in this pass.
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light summer daypack; add an ice axe (and optionally microspikes) for residual snow slopes, especially in July.

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long single day via the PCT corridor (multiple trailhead options); treat as a full-day objective — precise round-trip mileage/hours not confirmed
requiredSkills: Class 2 scree/loose-rock scrambling
comfort with exposure on a narrow, exposed ridge crest
snow slope travel and self-arrest with an ice axe (early-season lingering snow)
route-finding off the PCT onto the unofficial/spur summit path
afternoon-thunderstorm awareness and turnaround discipline on the exposed crest
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate scrambler comfortable with sustained Class 2 terrain, loose scree, and an exposed ridge crest near the top; not a beginner's first scramble given the crest exposure.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strenuous, long day - extended approach on the Taylor River/Snoqualmie Lake trail followed by off-trail gain to Preacher's slopes; expect a full day or overnight effort
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light day-climbing kit (~15-20 lb) for a single push; add overnight gear if camping along the approach to shorten the summit day

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long - full trail approach plus off-trail ascent; realistically a long single day or a backpack-in/climb-out over two days (exact route-specific mileage/time not confirmed in sources)
requiredSkills: Off-trail routefinding / navigation (map, compass, or GPS)
Class 2-3 scrambling on loose rock
Brush/bushwhacking travel tolerance
Sound judgment around afternoon thunderstorms (early start, turnaround discipline)
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate scrambler comfortable with sustained off-trail routefinding and Class 3 rock; not a beginner objective given the leave-the-trail approach and loose/brushy terrain

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very strong — capable of sustained 10-15+ mile approach days with major elevation gain on and off trail; reported link-up days to this peak involve ~10,500 ft gain over 15+ hours
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Multi-day backcountry load, roughly 30-45 lbs, to reach a central-Pasayten high camp before the summit push

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long — typically a 2-3 day round trip from Slate Peak or Eightmile Creek trailheads to a central-Pasayten high camp, then a ridge/talus scramble day to the summit
requiredSkills: off-trail navigation and route-finding
multi-day backcountry camping/self-sufficiency
loose talus and Class 2-3 scrambling
backcountry stream crossings
weather judgment for afternoon thunderstorms on an exposed ridge
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Advanced backcountry mountaineer/scrambler — needs multi-day wilderness self-sufficiency and off-trail routefinding, not just Class 2-3 scrambling ability, given the remote central-Pasayten approach and self-rescue distance called out in existing beta

fitnessSpec.hiking: Long wilderness approach fitness - full-day (or overnight) endurance typical of Glacier Peak Wilderness access; exact approach mileage not confirmed in sources
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light scrambling kit for the ridge itself; overnight/backpacking load (roughly 20-30 lb) likely needed for the approach given the remote access

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long/remote approach consistent with Glacier Peak Wilderness (Okanogan-Wenatchee NF) access
requiredSkills: route-finding on an unmaintained approach and along the ridge crest
exposed Class 3 scrambling, including negotiating rock steps and notches
sound judgment downclimbing loose rock
map/compass or GPS navigation in trail-less Glacier Peak Wilderness terrain
roped glacier travel and crevasse rescue
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid, independent Class 3 scrambler comfortable on an infrequently traveled ridge with loose rock and no fixed protection; not a beginner objective given the remote Glacier Peak Wilderness setting

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong hiker fitness — ~12 mi round trip with ~4,000+ ft gain from Cascade Pass TH to the summit, typically done car-to-car in a long day or as an overnight to Sahale Glacier Camp
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Day-pack for a single push; overnight pack (~30-35 lb with glacier gear) if camping at Sahale Glacier Camp

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~4-6 hrs hiking from Cascade Pass TH to Sahale Glacier Camp; summit day adds a few more hours over the glacier and summit block
requiredSkills: roped glacier travel
crevasse rescue basics
Class 3 scrambling on the summit block
self-arrest/basic snow travel for early-season snow
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Good for a motivated glacier-climbing novice/intermediate — widely cited as an entry-level North Cascades glacier route, but partner should be comfortable roped glacier travel and basic crevasse rescue since hidden crevasses are present

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high - reference trip reports log ~34 miles round trip with ~14,000 ft cumulative gain/loss over 3-4 days, much of it off-trail with brushy route-finding
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Multi-day overnight/glacier kit (35-50 lb): tent, food for 3-4 days, rope, glacier gear, bivy gear for weather delays

partner_requirements.approachTime: 2-3 days in, typically done as part of a 3-4 day trip (often combined with Dome Peak)
requiredSkills: Glacier travel and crevasse rescue (Chickamin/Dome Glacier crossing)
Steep snow/neve climbing and self-arrest (up to 45-50 degrees below the col)
Class 3 scrambling on loose rock with exposure
Off-trail navigation and bushwhack route-finding on the approach
Multi-day backcountry/wilderness travel and self-sufficiency
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine climber comfortable with unroped Class 3 scrambling on loose rock plus roped glacier travel; this is not a beginner objective given the remoteness and multi-day approach

fitnessSpec.approach: ~2.5 mi / ~2,000 ft gain from the Blue Lake trailhead

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~2.5 mi / ~2,000 ft gain from the Blue Lake trailhead
requiredSkills: Mostly 3rd/4th class with one 5.5 crux pitch, climbed first
Comfort with exposure on an airy, broad/broken knife-edge ridge
Basic routefinding — the broken ridge is easy to wander off of
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Beginner-friendly — commonly cited as a good first alpine rock lead

requiredSkills: Comfort with an approximate, not precisely documented route line
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: 5.4-5.6 trad leader

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~1.5–2 hrs (inferred/shared with neighboring routes, not route-specific-confirmed)
requiredSkills: Lower pitches ('funky 10a') shared with Direct East Buttress
Headwall is sustained, thin technical 5.11d corner cracks
Belays on the headwall are vague/unfixed — must be comfortable building solid gear anchors, not clipping bolted stations
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Confident 5.11 crack/corner climber comfortable building your own belays

fitnessSpec.hiking: Sustained forested approach plus off-trail slope gain to ~5600 ft with brush and elevation gain typical of Cascade foothill approaches
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light day pack (~15-20 lb) sufficient for a single-day scramble

partner_requirements.approachTime: Not separately verified in sources; expect a multi-hour forested approach typical of Index-area peaks before reaching open south-facing slopes
requiredSkills: Off-trail route-finding through dense brush and cliff bands
Loose rock / talus management and careful foot placement
Basic scrambling movement on heather and easy rock bands (Class 3)
Ability to reverse route-finding decisions if cliffed out
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid Class 3 scrambling experience with comfort on loose rock and route-finding through cliff bands without a marked trail; not a beginner objective

fitnessSpec.carToCar: ~8 hrs of climbing, plus the approach and descent

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~1 hr via the Blue Lake Trail and climbers' path to the base of the South Arete, then a short traverse down and right along the base of the wall past The Passenger's start; descent is a downclimb plus 3 rappels down South Arete, ~1 hr
requiredSkills: Mixed dihedrals, thin slabs, flakes, and roofs
~20 bolts but still needs a real trad rack (doubles to 2", 60m rope)
One documented party needed an aider on a section — be ready for occasional aid if needed
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid 5.11 trad/face leader

fitnessSpec.hiking: Multi-day approach fitness required - Terror Basin/Crescent Creek Basin access involves 6,000+ ft of gain on unmaintained, bushwhacky, route-finding-heavy terrain typical of Southern Pickets approaches
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight/multi-day pack (commonly cited around 40-50 lb for Southern Pickets trips) for camp gear plus a rock rack for the short technical section

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-day trip (typically one long day in to Terror Basin, then the Barrier crossing toward Crescent Creek Basin) before the short summit push; not a single-push day route
requiredSkills: Class 3-4 scrambling with a few low 5th-class moves on loose/choss rock
snow travel and snow-to-rock transitions (often reported as undercut/awkward)
off-trail alpine navigation and route-finding in glaciated/talus terrain
comfort with sustained exposure on a remote, rescue-unfriendly objective
basic self-rescue and glacier/crevasse awareness for the approach
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine climber with prior North Cascades choss/loose-rock mileage; this is not a beginner or intermediate objective given the remote approach and Grade III commitment

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high - parties describe a long, sustained single-day push from the Hidden Lake Trailhead across brushy, off-trail terrain and a glacier crossing; expect a full mountain day of 10+ hours car-to-car
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Moderate-to-heavy - full glacier travel kit (rope, crevasse-rescue gear), a light rock rack, and a 60m rope; no overnight camping gear is needed for the standard single-day car-to-car push

partner_requirements.approachTime: Single day - two documented trip reports both climb it car-to-car from the Hidden Lake Trailhead in roughly 10.5 hours; an approach camp is optional, not required, for the standard route
requiredSkills: glacier travel and crevasse rescue
roped travel / simul-climbing on 4th class to 5.4 terrain
remote alpine route-finding
comfort on loose, exposed rock
self-arrest and general snow travel
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine climber/mountaineer with prior roped glacier-travel trips - not a suitable first alpine objective

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong, sustained fitness for a long off-trail day: roughly 7-8 miles round trip with about 6,000 ft of total gain, much of it unmaintained tread, brush, and loose talus
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light day pack (~10-20 lbs) - water, layers, navigation tools; no technical rack needed for a Class 2-3 scramble

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long day - climb a faint, unsigned path up Green Ridge from the Middle Fork road, then travel cross-country past several lakes to a steep, loose scramble to the summit; full car-to-car outing likely runs 8-12+ hours given the off-trail terrain
requiredSkills: Off-trail routefinding/navigation (map, compass, and/or GPS) - approach relies on a faint, unofficial path
Class 3 scrambling on loose rock
Comfort with dense brush/bushwhacking
Sound judgment to retreat if afternoon thunderstorms build
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Advanced - this is described by route sources as suitable only for climbers with years of off-trail mountain travel experience, not a beginner scramble

fitnessSpec.hiking: Fit enough for a technical off-trail approach carrying a rock rack, rope, and rappel gear to the base of Ares Tower
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Moderate - rack, rope(s), helmet, approach shoes/rock shoes, rappel/rescue gear, layers for exposed afternoon weather

partner_requirements.approachTime: Not specified in existing beta; treat as a multi-hour technical approach from the Washington Pass / Silver Star area to the base of Ares Tower (verify current approach beta before attempting)
requiredSkills: Leading one short, exposed low-5th-class step and building a belay on alpine granite
Route-finding on featured, ledgy, occasionally loose alpine granite
A single rappel from a fixed summit anchor, including checking the anchor before weighting it
Comfort with exposure on technical pitches
Basic self-rescue / ability to bail given loose rock and afternoon thunderstorm risk
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid alpine scrambler at home on exposed, loose 4th-class ridge terrain and able to lead a short low-5th-class step, with route-finding on featured but sometimes loose granite; prior experience on the Washington Pass towers helps
